summary:
The SP category is the story of the week — R1, R2, and R3 are all riding 4-game winning streaks on starting pitcher-driven picks, with R1/R2 hot at +5.5pts over baseline (57% at n=171 over the last 14 days vs 52% season). That's the single most trustworthy lens on the board today, and it lines up cleanly with two of the strongest consensus plays: MIL over TEX (all four ratings stacked +2.12 to +2.60, Henderson at home favored over Bradford) and the MIA fade at Washington, where every rating hates the Marlins by at least -1.95 with Eury Pérez on the mound against Jackson Kent. Those two are as close to auto-plays as this board offers — full four-rating agreement plus the hot SP trend backing the framework that generated them.

Away from the extremes, trends+runs remains the best category combo all season (56.5%, 273-210, n=483) and trends+sp is right behind at 56.4% — both categories are humming hot right now, and CHC over CIN and NYY over BOS are consensus plays that fit that same trends-driven mold, worth full confidence. Watch the team trends too: BOS is a brutal 79% (34-9) when the model likes them straight up, but today it's fading Boston against the Yankees, which cuts against that team leader — a spot where the SP/trend signal should override the team-name bias. TBR remains a strong-play machine (19-6, +21.0u when flagged strong) but today's TBR pick vs SDP is thin, R1 barely above breakeven at +0.09 — treat it as a lean, not a strong play. Skip the split boards: PHI@LAA (R1-R3 like LAA, R4 flips to PHI) and KCR@CLE (three ratings split within 0.12 of dead even) offer no edge and should be passed regardless of what R4's small-sample hot streak (60% season, n=86) suggests elsewhere.
